To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the first order in a series expansion of the covariance and bias of a maximum-likelihood estimator in terms of inverse power of SNR, where the square root is the CRLB, can be used to estimate errors of physical parameters in GW signals from binary mergers.

the first order expansion of the covariance of a maximum likelihood estimator is a better estimate than the CRLR bound and that the necessary signal to noise ratio to get an error close to the CRLB is larger than the kurtosis of the signal spectrum.

the Cramer Rao bound (CRB) is a lower bound on the error of a maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) for a single interferometer only if the signal-to-noiseratio (SNR) is large enough and the dimensionality of the parameter space is small enough.

the study of the properties of the gravitational waves emitted during the inspiral phase and their detection by interferometric gravitational wave detectors.
the application of the theory of asymptotic expansions of errors in parameter estimation to gravitational waves.

the methodology developed here is a powerful tool to understand the relationship between the SNR, the waveform, the dimension of the parameter estimation space and the errors in the maximum likelihood estimates.

the methodology developed here, based on expansions of the covariance of maximum likelihood estimates, is a powerful tool for the study of GW parameter estimation errors, especially when numerical simulations are not available.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the first two orders in the expansion of the covariance are sufficient to approximate the error of a maximum likelihood estimator for GW signals in a noise background of a GW interferometer and the expansion can also predict the necessary SNR to reach the CRLB.
the CRLB is a useful approximation to errors for maximum likelihood estimation only when the SNR is sufficiently large.

we have developed a new frequentist method to calculate analytical errors for maximum likelihood estimations of physical parameters for GWs from the inspiral phases of binary systems in the noise of a single interferometer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the first two orders in the asymptotic expansions of the error for a single interferometer are sufficient to get good predictions of the error.
for a given SNR, the error of an unbiased maximum likelihood estimate of the parameters of a gravitational wave signal is smaller than the CRLBs.
, for a single interferometer, we can get a better understanding of estimation errors for gravitational waves from binary systems by using the first two order expansions.
